page: OVHcloud h100-380 is a cloud GPU instance built on KVM virtualization, engineered primarily for deep learning acceleration, large-scale model inference, and data-intensive compute workloads. The system is equipped with 30 dedicated physical x86_64 cores from the AMD EPYC 9354 processor running at 3.0 GHz, configured without simultaneous multithreading (1 thread per core). Memory allocation stands at 380.0 GB of system RAM, providing an ample 12.67 GB per core. The host also integrates a dedicated NVIDIA Hopper H100 accelerator offering 80 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM, 4,040 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Complementary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier execution in GPU-centric operations. In large language model inference tests across 135M, 7B, and 70B parameter models, the instance consistently scores in the top 10% for both prompt processing and token generation, processing 4,640.67 prompt tokens per second and generating 201.78 tokens per second on 7B models. On CPU-driven benchmarks, the AMD EPYC 9354 delivers strong performance with a single-core stress-ng result of 3,147.58 (top 10%) and a multi-core score of 94,563.21 (top 25%). Cache performance is robust with cached small-block read speeds reaching 4,405.2 GB/sec, alongside high Redis SET throughput of 72.92 million operations per second.

Performance tradeoffs emerge within host memory subsystem bandwidth and general CPU execution. Large-block uncached memory read and write benchmarks register in the bottom 25% at 30.58 GB/sec and 22.36 GB/sec, respectively. In addition, multi-core Geekbench ratings (14,257.0) and database operations (21,233.72) hover in the middle 50%, reflecting limits in host RAM streaming compared to pure accelerator throughput. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server combines high hardware density by packaging a flagship datacenter GPU with extensive local NVMe capacity and dedicated EPYC cores, maximizing resource value for heavy accelerator tasks rather than pure host memory bandwidth applications.

The OVHcloud h100-380 is optimal for training and fine-tuning medium-sized machine learning models, deploying high-throughput LLM inference APIs, scientific simulation frameworks, and GPU-accelerated ETL pipelines requiring rapid local NVMe staging.
description: OVHcloud h100-380 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance featuring a single NVIDIA Hopper H100 accelerator with 80 GB VRAM. The instance is powered by 30 dedicated physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9354 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz, 380 GB of system RAM, and 4,040 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage over an 8 Gbps network interface. Benchmark results indicate exceptional performance in AI workloads, placing the instance in the top 10% for LLM prompt processing and token generation across small, medium, and 70B parameter models. Host compute is reinforced by strong single-thread CPU benchmarks and AVX-512 support, though uncached large-block RAM throughput remains relatively modest. The generous combination of local NVMe capacity and Hopper acceleration positions this instance effectively for high-throughput LLM inference, machine learning model training, and data-heavy scientific computing.
